First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

We rewrite the given expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta }{1-{sec}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta }{1-(1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta }{1-1-{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =-\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =-\frac{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta }{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =-\frac{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }\cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta }{\cancel{{tan}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & =-\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{tan}^{3}⁡\theta }{1-{sec}^{2}⁡\theta }=-\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta .
$$
